## AC integrity gate outcome

**Result:** pass, with one workflow-stage drop. There is no hard stop, no park, and no relocation.

| Row | Class | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| The PR description lists every deleted test file | Workflow-stage proof. Its only observable is the pull request's description, which is a delivery artifact, not a behavior of the change. | **Dropped.** The text is kept verbatim in the Reporter note under `retired workflow-stage proof:`. |
| The retired parser's test directory is empty after its obsolete tests are removed | Behavioral and binary. Setup: the retired parser's test directory. Action: remove the obsolete tests. Result: the directory is empty. It can be verified before production. | **Kept** byte-for-byte. |
| The release script writes the changelog section into the pull request body | Behavioral. The release script's own behavior is the observable, even though it produces pull-request text. This is the explicit keep case. | **Kept** byte-for-byte. |

**Normalization:** both surviving rows were already `- [ ]` items. No checkbox, wording, or setup/action framing changed.

**AC uniqueness:** no row's observable is contained in another row, and no row bundles independent observations. Nothing was removed or split beyond the stage-proof drop.

**Deploy window:** both surviving rows can be fulfilled before production. The list is not empty, so there is no no-AC failure.

**Mode consequence:** the drop changes the AC section, so this is a substantive full-replacement repair, not a conformance-only byte lock. The no-op check does not apply because the body changes and a comment is proposed. The approved payload will be the body plus this one Reporter-note comment.
